newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 1.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - According to the Czech Medical Chamber's decision on Sunday, emergency doctors can begin taking payments from patients in cash from today, because doctors did not reach an agreement with insurance companies.
- The trading company Metalimex a.s. will pay dividends from 1996 profits of 500 crowns per each 1,000-crown share.

- The year-on-year decrease in industrial sales in May by 0.7 percent surprised many experts who expected another significant increase in prices. After taking out the fact that there was one less working day in May, the actual increase amounts to 1.5 percent.
- A new law on spirits will go into effect today, which sets new conditions for manufacturing, storing and sale of spirits.

- On the agenda for the July parliament meeting, which begins this afternoon, are the cabinet's report on its activities since last year's elections, a discussion on the second budget cuts of 42 billion crowns, changes to tax laws and new social legislature.
- The German concern GEA AG will increase its current stake in Liberecke Vzduchotechnicke Zavody of 76 percent by another 15 percent.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Prime Minister and leader of ODS Vaclav Klaus surprisingly met with two adversaries of the cabinet yesterday, Republican representatives Josef Krejsa and Petr Vrzan, who said they spoke about many issues, including the central bank and the cabinet's package.

- From today, living expenses in the Czech Republic will increase significantly, rents by 20 to 100 percent, electricity and gas by 15 percent, heating by up to 39 percent, radio payments by 10 crowns and television by 25 crowns.
- Former Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, who just last week became a board member of Ceska Pojistovna, was yesterday voted in as chairman of the board of this insurance company.
- On June 27, the budget deficit was 18.2 billion crowns, and revenue developments show that many companies misused their money which was to go to the state as taxes.
- The Czech National Bank would welcome a government budget next year with a surplus of around three percent of GDP, much larger than planned by Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik.
- Several wine companies are increasing their prices today, due to this year's weak harvest, Vinium by up to 15 percent, Znovin on average by 2.50 crowns per 0.7 litre.

PRAVO - CSOB bank decreased its base rate by one percentage point to 19 percent yesterday and its prime rate by one percent to 18 percent. From July 1, Komercni Banka is increasing its interest rates for crown accounts of more than six months tied to the reference rate.
- From today, Ceska Rafinerska is decreasing its prices, motor oil by 150 crowns per tonne and petrol by 100 crowns.
- On Monday, the Czech National Bank decreased its repo rate to 18.20 percent. The crown traded at around 18.6 to the mark.
- The balance sum of the Czech National Bank decreased by more than 23 billion crowns to 625.641 billion crowns from June 10 to 20 this year.
- The planned merger of Chemopetrol Group and Kaucuk Group with state-owned Unipetrol was delayed. Chemopetrol Group was not delisted yesterday, which was one of the conditions of the merger.

LIDOVE NOVINY - A new law on state businesses goes into effect today, which will restrict their activities as in many foreign countries. The law should react to the changing situation with ownership relations.

- The American embassy and Chemapol Group signed a grant contract between the United States government, represented by the Trade and Development Agency, and Koramo Kolin. TDA will issue Koramo a grant of $200,000, the first grant issued by the U.S. government to a private company in the Czech Republic.
- From July 1, today, citizens can request no-interest state loans for housing and mortgage credits with progressively increasing payments.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus admitted yesterday that, in connection to Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik's leaving the government, he seriously considered whether or not to leave the cabinet himself.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
